findings.description: The reports_archive bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects are stored with S3 default encryption settings rather than an explicitly enforced KMS-managed key, leaving report data unprotected by customer-controlled encryption.
The ledger_exports bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving exported financial ledger objects without explicitly configured encryption at rest.
The model_artifacts bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so stored model artifacts are not explicitly encrypted with a managed key.
The ops_runbooks bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving operational runbook content unencrypted by explicit policy.

findings.issue_category: permissive ACL grants log delivery write
findings.description: The audit bucket is configured with acl = "log-delivery-write", a canned legacy ACL that grants write access to the S3 log delivery group; this broadens access to a bucket holding security audit logs.

The model_artifacts logging block sends access logs to the audit_trail bucket with no target encryption of its own; this is acceptable, but the configuration commits log data to a bucket whose access controls are widened by a log-delivery-write ACL.
